import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Income distribution by education level
income_edu = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].median().sort_values(ascending=False)
bars1 = axes[0, 0].bar(range(len(income_edu)), income_edu.values, color=sns.color_palette("husl", len(income_edu)))
axes[0, 0].set_title('Median Income by Education Level', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Median Income ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_xticks(range(len(income_edu)))
axes[0, 0].set_xticklabels(income_edu.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
for i, (bar, value) in enumerate(zip(bars1, income_edu.values)):
    axes[0, 0].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 500, 
                   f'${value:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 2. Spending categories comparison
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 
                 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_totals = df[spending_cols].sum()
spending_labels = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
colors2 = sns.color_palette("Set2", len(spending_labels))
wedges, texts, autotexts = axes[0, 1].pie(spending_totals, labels=spending_labels, colors=colors2,
                                          autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, textprops={'fontsize': 10})
axes[0, 1].set_title('Total Spending by Category', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# 3. Purchase channels comparison
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_totals = df[purchase_cols].sum()
channels = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store']
x_pos = np.arange(len(channels))
bars3 = axes[1, 0].bar(x_pos, purchase_totals, color=sns.color_palette("viridis", len(channels)))
axes[1, 0].set_title('Total Purchases by Channel', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Purchase Channel', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Total Number of Purchases', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_xticks(x_pos)
axes[1, 0].set_xticklabels(channels)
for i, (bar, value) in enumerate(zip(bars3, purchase_totals)):
    axes[1, 0].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 50, 
                   f'{value:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

# 4. Customer demographics: Kids and Teens at home
family_data = df[['Kidhome', 'Teenhome']].sum()
family_labels = ['Kids at Home', 'Teens at Home']
colors4 = ['#FF9999', '#66B2FF']
bars4 = axes[1, 1].bar(family_labels, family_data, color=colors4)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Customer Family Composition', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Total Count', fontsize=12)
for i, (bar, value) in enumerate(zip(bars4, family_data)):
    axes[1, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 20, 
                   f'{value:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

# Adjust layout and add overall title
plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis: Demographics, Spending & Behavior', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close()
